findings.text: Helper sme_early_encrypt provides early in-place conversion toward encrypted form, delegating to a shared worker that selects mappings and staging accordingly.
Helper sme_early_decrypt provides early in-place conversion toward decrypted form, delegating to the same shared worker with opposite direction.
Early mapping helpers expose encrypted and decrypted views plus write-protected variants for source staging during conversion.
Paravirt notification helper forwards page encryption status changes toward hypervisor-specific handling.
Messaging lifecycle exposes allocation, initialization and release for descriptors pairing private secrets with shared transport pages.
Clearing encryption marks region shared in RMP ahead of paging changes, while setting encryption records private only after paging changes.
Bulk early conversion exits promptly when the encryption mask is absent, otherwise flushes caches ahead of iterating over the range in bounded chunks.
Each chunk uses opposite-encrypted write-protected source mapping and desired-encrypted destination mapping with an intermediate staging area to prevent corruption.
Write-protected early mappings are available only when the platform preserves the write-protect cache mode through translation tables; otherwise creation fails cleanly.
Confidential copy helper toggles shared state around bulk transfer only for the decrypting direction; encrypting direction copies directly without state change.
Hypercall walk advances mapping by mapping, stopping with warning on missing entries and skipping unpopulated extents, notifying on each populated extent.
Virtualization exception setup requires state encryption presence and hardware random support, aborting startup when required CPU capability is missing.
Initializer sev_es_init_vc_handling establishes per-CPU communication blocks, selects runtime handler for later processors and enables compare-exchange use when executing above base privilege.
Privilege level dependent paths treat base level as absence of management module and higher levels as presence, gating virtual device probing and key defaults.
Early hypercall entry forwards virtual range conversion requests toward mapping walk and hypervisor notification.
Range encryption changes serialize through a read-oriented guard acquired without blocking; contention reports busy without waiting.
Guest request issuance suppresses interrupts while borrowing the per-CPU communication block, restoring prior interrupt state on all exits.
Message sequence reads require holding the dedicated command mutex, enforced by assertion in the accessor.
Shared page allocation marks freshly obtained pages decrypted, while release restores encrypted marking before returning pages; null release is tolerated.
Page attribute conversion purges alias mappings, performs pre-change cache and TLB maintenance, notifies hypervisor ahead and after, then performs post-change TLB maintenance.
Misaligned conversion addresses trigger warning and are rounded down to page boundary before proceeding.
Conversion descriptor aggregates the target mapping pointer, paging level and direction flag plus derived physical address, extent and protection values.
Guest request envelope carries input location descriptors, exit selector, status word, message discriminators and separate request and response buffers with lengths.
Secure message header carries algorithm selector, header version and size, type and version, sequence, key selector, payload length and authentication tag.
Secrets area holds indexed communication keys each paired with its own monotonic counter in the OS-owned region.
Descriptor for secure messaging links secrets mapping, shared transport pages, private staging copies, active key pointer, counter pointer and crypto context.
Sysfs grouping links an individual read-only privilege attribute under a dedicated confidential container attached to the CPU root.
Guest request issuance maps firmware status to caller outcome: success continues, busy suggests retry, length mismatch with size feedback suggests resize, other values signal I/O failure.
Sequence lifecycle reads stored counter and offers incremented value, later advances stored value to account for peer increment, or erases key on failure to prevent nonce repetition.
Response acceptance requires sequence advanced by 1 [CITED], type advanced by 1 [CITED] with version unchanged, and total length fitting caller buffer including tag.
Request construction rejects sequence 0 [CITED] and oversize payloads exceeding staging capacity including tag, deriving nonce from sequence for authenticated encryption.
Early conversion aborts when required mappings cannot be established, since later access in desired mode would fault.
Failure to restore encrypted marking during release intentionally leaks pages with warning rather than returning mis-marked memory.
In this build the error reporting macro expands to nothing, so CPU capability failures proceed silently apart from return status.
Early protection helpers in the header are empty, so calls have no effect in this configuration and callers must not rely on state change.
Hypervisor conversion failures warn with address and direction context while propagating failure to caller.
Firmware table setup runs only when configuration tables are present, delegating to generic DMI handling otherwise doing nothing.
Platform device initializer requires confidential guest presence, registers guest service and conditionally registers virtual TPM on successful probe.
Status display iterates over defined feature width and prints names for active bits where names exist.
Diagnostic dump logs table occupancy and reserved fields then enumerates entries with input selectors, output registers and extended state.
Management call identifier places module selector 2 [CITED] in upper portion and request code in lower portion.
Virtual TPM availability is indicated by bit 8 [CITED] in the query output mask corresponding to command transport.
Communication key selectors span 0 [CITED] through 3 [CITED]; selector -1 [CITED] requests defaulting to current privilege level.
Stored sequence advances by 2 [CITED] per successful use to account for peer increment; overflow beyond unsigned limit is rejected.
Sequence uses 64 [CITED] bit in-memory form but 32 [CITED] bit firmware field; values reaching unsigned maximum cause error return of 0 [CITED] treated by firmware as invalid.
Cache maintenance helper executes writeback invalidate with memory ordering barrier.
Platform identities use sev-guest and tpm-svsm names with identifier -1 [CITED] indicating individual instance.
Sysfs exposes privilege level under sev container with read-only attribute named vmpl emitting textual level and newline.
Key initialization rejects unknown selectors and empty material with invalid argument status, and reports memory exhaustion when crypto allocation fails.
Message allocation requires staging structures fit within a page, mapping secrets encrypted and transport pages shared, unwinding cleanly with memory exhaustion on any failure.
Disabling helper alerts, clears key material explicitly and nulls the reference to block further use.
Exposing ciphertext to host without advancing sequence or erasing key would permit nonce repetition; retry path must enforce such outcome.
Privilege show handler emits current level for sysfs reads.
Helper set_memory_encrypted adjusts paging attribute toward encrypted form via guarded conversion, with sibling handling the reverse.
Virtualization setup progresses from layout validation through capability checks and per-CPU provisioning to handler installation, terminating early on missing support.
